newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: DuPont to up Asia-Pacific investment - paper.
newsitem.headline: DuPont to up Asia-Pacific investment - paper.

text.p: DuPont Co plans to invest $1.5 billion in the Asia-Pacific region over the next five years, the Straits Times reported on Tuesday.

It said John Krol, DuPont's president and chief executive officer, told Singapore reporters on Monday the money would be invested in projects in China, India, Malaysia, Indonesia and Singapore. DuPont officials confirmed the report.
Krol, in Singapore as part of a tour of DuPont's facilities in Southeast Asia, said the company would build a second fibre plant in western Singapore at a cost of Singapore $140 million next year.
The city-state is also being considered, along with China and Malaysia, as a possible site for a US$750 million nylon intermediate, hexamethylene diamine plant.
Krol said the Asia-Pacific region was DuPont's fastest growing market with sales growth of 20 percent annually. Total sales in the region reached US$3.5 billion last year.
He said the region accounted for about seven percent of DuPont's global sales currently, but the company aimed to raise this stake to 20 percent, with sales of US$9 billion by the end of the decade.
Krol said he expected two-thirds of DuPont's worldwide sales to be generated outside North America in the next 10 years.
Half the company's annual sales of US$42 billion are currently generated outside North America.
